name: Community associations and clubs
sector: 7.M Digital economy, social and public sector

problems.words: Many members are behind on dues and we chase manually
quick_ideas: Bring every member code's dues status into one list, so you see the full picture
Send one polite, general reminder to all units in arrears rather than individual chasing.

workzap_build.text: a dues ledger by member code with automated WhatsApp and email reminders and payment links.

problems.ask_first: How do members usually pay their dues at the moment?
problems.free_stops: The reminder schedule and ledger set-up are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many dues reminders go out each week and how many payments follow, so manual chasing effort is easier to judge.
Give one person a fixed weekly time to update the arrears list in one notebook, so follow-up stays regular and calm.

problems.words: Payments come by cash, cheque and transfer and we can't match them
quick_ideas: Ask members to quote their member or unit code as the transfer reference
Match the bank statement against the ledger on one fixed day each month.

workzap_build.text: a payment matcher linking transfers, cash and cheques to member codes directly.

problems.ask_first: Do most members pay cash at the office, or by transfer into the bank account?
problems.free_stops: The matching rules are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each payment note with the same day's cash, cheque and transfer records once this week, so the mismatch point stands out.
Give one staff member one notebook for every payment received that day, so matching stops being split across different places.

problems.words: Court bookings on WhatsApp lead to fights over slots
quick_ideas: Keep one booking calendar that only one person can confirm
Publish simple slot rules, so everyone plays by the same ones.

workzap_build.text: You would see court, hall, pool and barbecue slots booked from one place, with slot rules applied and only members able to reserve.

problems.ask_first: Do the fights come over popular evening slots, or over bookings that were never confirmed?
problems.free_stops: The slot rules and booking flow are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many court slot requests clash with existing bookings this week, so the busiest times and arguments become clearer.
Give one person the job of confirming every court slot in one written list, so members hear one answer about availability.

problems.words: The WhatsApp group is chaos, important notices get buried
quick_ideas: Start an announcements-only channel separate from the chat group
Pin key notices so new members can find them.

workzap_build.text: a notice broadcast channel that keeps announcements apart from chatter, with delivery to every member.

problems.ask_first: Is the chaos mostly chat between members, or mostly committee notices getting buried?
problems.free_stops: The broadcast set-up goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many important notices are repeated because members missed them this week, so the cost of buried messages is clearer.
Give one staff member a fixed time to post all notices in one place daily, so updates stop getting scattered through chat.

problems.words: New committee every year, records don't get handed over
quick_ideas: List every record, contract and account access the committee relies on
Store them under the association's control, not on personal phones.

workzap_build.text: a handover pack keeping records and contracts under the association's control with role-based access.

problems.ask_first: Do records vanish when the old committee leaves, or were they never written down in the first place?
problems.free_stops: The handover structure and access roles are prepared in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk through current committee work and note every record still sitting on personal phones or papers, so handover risks are easier to see.
Give one committee member the job of keeping one master handover list, so incoming members receive the same records every time.

quick_ideas: Keep income and spending categorised monthly, not only at year-end
Agree with your accountant the format they need well before the AGM.

problems.words: Security guards don't do rounds and nobody can check
quick_ideas: Agree the rounds and times with the guards openly
Ask the guard supervisor for a simple daily rounds report.

workzap_build.text: You would see guards scanning set checkpoints on their rounds with times recorded, alongside staff attendance, all used openly with the guards.

Review it at every committee meeting until each is closed.

problems.words: Event ticket money collected by volunteers in cash, never reconciled
quick_ideas: Count event cash with two people before anyone leaves
Compare the count with tickets sold the same evening.

workzap_build.text: event ticketing with QR entry and sales reconciled to cash at close.

problems.words: Canteen loses money and we don't know why
quick_ideas: Count canteen cash and key stock at close for a week
Compare what was bought with what was sold for the top items.

workzap_build.text: a canteen stock and sales tracker with a daily morning read of cash and stock.

problems.ask_first: Does the canteen lose money mostly on stock that goes missing, or on prices set too low?
problems.free_stops: The tracker and daily read are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which canteen items run out early and which sit unsold this week, so waste and missed sales show up clearly.

never_say: Advice on bylaws, elections, strata or owners'-association law, or legal action against defaulters — say "talk to a lawyer".
Taking sides in committee politics or elections.
Publicly naming or shaming defaulters, or asking for member names, unit numbers, plates or bank details.
Help falsifying AGM accounts, rigging elections or hiding funds.

sample_reply.person: I'm treasurer for our owners' association. Owners are late on service charges and I chase them one by one. Can you help?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be fixed, and the first steps are simple.
First, bring every unit code's payment status into one list, so you can see the whole picture at once.
Second, ask owners to quote their unit code as the transfer reference, so payments match without guesswork.
Workzap could build this for you: a dues ledger that matches each payment to its unit and sends reminders on schedule.

Would you like me to prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
